title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR used as Charles Martel: a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours, and Frankish/generic hero alternatives were available in the editor
SALADIN used as Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi: an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of the 1170s-80s, wrong dynasty, wrong century, wrong theatre (Levant, not Iberia/Gaul)
EL_CID used as Duke Odo of Aquitaine: an 11th-century Castilian, and ironically a figure who fought Muslim and Christian rulers in Iberia, not an 8th-century Aquitanian duke

Umayyad camp built as a stone CASTLE with 99 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE and 4 GUARD_TOWERS: Abd al-Rahman's force was a mobile raiding army with a wagon/tent laager, not a masonry fortress in the Loire valley
PIKEMAN x8 in the Frankish line: the pike square is a 14th-century development; Man-at-Arms/Spearman would have covered the 8th-century Frankish infantry adequately
CAMEL_RIDER x12 as the core of the invading force: Umayyad armies in Gaul fought as horse cavalry; camel troops are an out-of-region flourish
MONASTERY for Player Two's Muslim army: Christian monastic architecture assigned to the Umayyad camp
